subject: HealthPrime API untethering: discovery notes & model shortlist
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Alex Donovan <alex.donovan@healthprime.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: HealthPrime API untethering: discovery notes & model shortlist

Alex — thanks for the time earlier. Quick recap from my side so we have a shared record and clear next steps. I pulled together the items we discussed plus a preliminary shortlist of model variants that look like good fits for your workloads. Attachments: healthprime-usage-snapshot.csv (traffic by endpoint, token distributions), call-recording-20260801.mp3, initial-poc-outline.pdf.

High-level pain points you called out
- Rising per-token spend from current OpenAI GPT-4 + Anthropic consumption (esp. high-volume billing on /summarize and /chat endpoints).
- Latency variability during spikes (90th pct latency currently ~420ms; goal <= 120ms for customer-facing routes).
- Model alignment drift on internal prompts: certain clinical summarization prompts produce hallucinations ~6-8% of time.
- Procurement and compliance: must maintain HIPAA-safe handling, enterprise KMS integration, and audit logs for data residency.

Current stack we captured
- Frontend -> API gateway -> proprietary LLM vendor endpoints (OpenAI/Anthropic) for chat & summarization.
- Service-layer transforms requests to vendor-specific call patterns (function-calls, structured outputs).
- Batch offline reranking with a small internal ensemble.
- Traffic: ~5M tokens/day today, peaks to 12M tokens/day on heavy days per the attached snapshot.

Success criteria for a migration/POC (measurable)
- Latency: tail latency (95th) for user-facing chat <= 150ms end-to-end (we recommend aiming for <=120ms target later).
- Cost: token cost delta <= 40% vs current baseline after Redwood optimizations (caching, batching, quantized runtimes).
- Fidelity: reduction in hallucination rate to <= 2% on your clinical summary eval suite (we'll run your eval set).
- API compatibility: minimal changes to request/response contract; support for your current function-calling schema expected.

Compatibility & constraints you emphasized
- Must preserve current function-calling pattern (name + JSON schema) and streaming behavior for the chat flows.
- PHI content: all inference must be encrypted in transit and at rest; keys managed through your KMS (GCP KMS in your case).
- Auditability: request-level logs retained for 180 days in your VPC (or we can ship them to your S3).

Preliminary model shortlist (we will benchmark these during the POC)
- Llama-2-Chat-70B (quantized 4-bit): strong cost/quality balance for instruction-like chat; good for function-calling after light fine-tuning.
- Mistral-Chat-8x: leaner latency profile, promising for streaming and lower memory footprint.
- RedPajama-Chat-3B (ensembling candidate): low-cost reranker / lightweight summarizer fallback.
- Redwood-curated medium-latency variant (service-managed): offers an SLA-backed option if you want a managed swap-in.

Proposed POC plan (2–3 weeks) & owners
1) Week 0 (this week): exchange artifacts — you provide sample payloads, evaluation prompts, HIPAA questionnaire answers, and a short list of top 200 API calls. Owner: HealthPrime (Alex). Due: 2026-08-05.
2) Week 1: Redwood runs offline evals on your eval set + small online canary in our sandbox (non-PHI tokens only) to validate semantics & latency. Owner: Redwood (Sergio/Ben). Deliverable: initial metrics dashboard + model comparison. Due: 2026-08-12.
3) Week 2: Controlled live canary (VPC/Dedicated path) with production-like traffic shaping and telemetry. Owner: HealthPrime + Redwood. Deliverable: production runbook, cost projection, and decision go/no-go. Due: 2026-08-21.

Immediate asks from Redwood to you
- A sanitized sample of 200 representative requests (or a redacted subset) and the evaluation prompts you use for clinical summaries.
- Confirmation of KMS provider and whether we can provision a temporary test key for the sandbox.
- Point of contact for legal/procurement (so we can share a targeted SOW).

Quick risks we want to call out up front
- Any on-call rollback plan needs to consider differences in tokenization across models (we'll provide mapping and token normalization guidance).
- Function-calling fidelity: some models will require a small adapter layer to maintain exact JSON shapes — this is low-effort but worth budgeting.

Next steps (agreed on the call)
- Alex to share the sample payloads + HIPAA questionnaire by 2026-08-05.
- Redwood to deliver the first eval report by 2026-08-12.
- Schedule a security deep-dive with your SREs (Lauren to propose times).

If this captures everything, we'll start the artifact exchange and spin up the initial offline evals. Thanks again — good conversation and strong alignment on the priority list.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0127

---
Attachments: healthprime-usage-snapshot.csv (csv), call-recording-20260801.mp3 (audio), initial-poc-outline.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Donovan <alex.donovan@healthprime.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: HealthPrime Platform Team <platform@healthprime.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: HealthPrime API untethering: discovery notes & model shortlist

Thanks, Sergio — that summary is perfect and very helpful. A couple quick clarifications: 
- We can provide a redacted sample set by EOD 2026-08-05. I will remove PHI and include the eval prompts you requested.
- On latency: the 120ms goal is aspirational; our immediate bar is 150ms for the chat front-line routes. If you can show a path to 120ms in 3 months that’s ideal.
- Procurement: our procurement lead (procurement@healthprime.com) will need a draft SOW/price band for the Dedicated option to review internally.

Also: are there any expected schema changes we should budget for on our side, or can the adapter layer be entirely Redwood-managed?

Appreciate the quick follow-up. I copied our platform team.

—Alex
Alex Donovan
Head of Platform Engineering | HealthPrime
alex.donovan@healthprime.com | +1 (617) 555-0142

Subject: Re: HealthPrime API untethering: discovery notes & model shortlist

Alex — great, thanks for the quick reply. Short answers: 
- Adapter layer: Redwood can manage the adapter and provide the shim so your engineers don't need to rewrite call sites; we'll surface any unavoidable contract diffs early in Week 1.
- SOW / price band: Ben will draft a targeted SOW and a price band for Dedicated vs Hosted POC by Tue 2026-08-04.
- Security deep-dive: Lauren will send a calendar invite for a 45-minute session with your SRE and our security/solutions folks (proposed: 2026-08-06 or 2026-08-07).

One more note: I'll also attach a short tokenization checklist we use — it helps teams understand where token mismatches can affect cost and score. Sending that in a follow-up thread; for now, expect the artifact exchange list above.

I'll mark the HubSpot deal (HP-3421) with the POC milestone and link the notes. If procurement wants an NDA/SOW faster, point them to procurement@redwood.com and Ben will prioritize.

Talk soon,
Sergio
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
